requirements.subject: ent:preprocessing-macro
requirements.canonical: A preprocessing macro IS a macro that a preprocessor or compiler replaces with a charstring or integer value before compilation.
requirements.original: A preprocessing macro is a macro that is replaced by a preprocessor or a compiler with a charstring or integer value respectively before compilation.

requirements.subject: ent:preprocessing-macro
requirements.canonical: A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a literal charstring value.
requirements.original: Preprocessing macros shall not be replaced inside literal charstring values and templates and not in TTCN-3 comments.

requirements.subject: ent:preprocessing-macro
requirements.canonical: A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a literal charstring template (e.g. a pattern string).
requirements.original: Preprocessing macros shall not be replaced inside literal charstring values and templates and not in TTCN-3 comments.

ambiguity.issue: "templates" is ambiguous: D.5 examples (D.5-s014) show __SCOPE__ being replaced in template definitions, so "templates" most likely means literal character string templates such as pattern strings. The canonical text chooses that reading.
readings: A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a literal charstring template such as a pattern string.
A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced anywhere inside a template definition.

requirements.subject: ent:preprocessing-macro
requirements.canonical: A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a TTCN-3 comment.
requirements.original: Preprocessing macros shall not be replaced inside literal charstring values and templates and not in TTCN-3 comments.

requirements.subject: ent:preprocessing-macro
requirements.canonical: A preprocessing macro MAY be used in TTCN-3 code wherever a charstring or integer value, respectively, can be used.
requirements.original: In the TTCN-3 code, it can be used like a charstring or an integer value respectively.

requirements.subject: ent:macro-module
requirements.canonical: The `__MODULE__` preprocessing macro denotes the name of the module in which the macro is used.
requirements.original: The __MODULE__ preprocessing macro denotes the module name in which the macro is used.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace every occurrence of `__MODULE__` with the actual module name as a charstring value.
requirements.original: A preprocessor or compiler shall replace all occurrences of __MODULE__ with the actual module name in form of a charstring value.

requirements.subject: ent:macro-file
requirements.canonical: The `__FILE__` preprocessing macro denotes the canonical (absolute) file name, i.e. the full path and the basic file name, of the file in which the macro is used.
requirements.original: The __FILE__ preprocessing macro denotes the canonical (absolute) file name, i.e. the full path and the basic file name, in which the macro is used.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace every occurrence of `__FILE__` with the actual canonical (absolute) file name as a charstring value.
requirements.original: A preprocessor or compiler shall replace all occurrences of __FILE__ with the actual canonical (absolute) file name in form of a charstring value.

requirements.subject: ent:file-name
requirements.canonical: The format of the canonical file name IS NOT specified by the standard and depends on the operating system.
requirements.original: NOTE: The format of the canonical file name depends on the operating system and is not specified by the present document.

requirements.subject: ent:macro-bfile
requirements.canonical: The `__BFILE__` preprocessing macro denotes the basic (relative) file name, i.e. without path, of the file in which the macro is used.
requirements.original: The __BFILE__ preprocessing macro denotes the basic (relative) file name, i.e. without path, in which the macro is used.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace every occurrence of `__BFILE__` with the actual basic (relative) file name as a charstring value.
requirements.original: A preprocessor or compiler shall replace all occurrences of __BFILE__ with the actual basic (relative) file name in form of a charstring value.

requirements.subject: ent:file-name
requirements.canonical: The format of the basic file name IS NOT specified by the standard and depends on the operating system.
requirements.original: NOTE: The format of the basic file name depends on the operating system and is not specified by the present document.

requirements.subject: ent:macro-line
requirements.canonical: The `__LINE__` preprocessing macro denotes the line number, in the file, of the line in which the macro is used.
requirements.original: The __LINE__ preprocessing macro denotes the line number of the file in which the macro is used.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace each occurrence of `__LINE__` with the actual line number as an integer value.
requirements.original: A preprocessor or compiler shall replace each occurrence of __LINE__ with the actual line number in form of an integer value.

requirements.subject: ent:line-number
requirements.canonical: The first line of a file IS line number 1.
requirements.original: A file starts with line number 1.

requirements.subject: ent:line-number
requirements.canonical: Each newline SHALL increase the line number by 1.
requirements.original: Each newline shall increase the line number by 1 (see clause A.1.5.1).

requirements.subject: ent:line-number
requirements.canonical: A newline inside a commented line SHALL also increase the line number by 1.
requirements.original: Also newlines of commented lines shall increase the line number by 1.

requirements.subject: ent:macro-scope
requirements.canonical: The `__SCOPE__` preprocessing macro denotes the unqualified name of the lowest named basic scope unit in which the macro is used.
requirements.original: The __SCOPE__ preprocessing macro denotes the unqualified name of the lowest named basic scope unit in which the macro is used.

requirements.subject: ent:scope-unit
requirements.canonical: The basic scope units of TTCN-3 ARE the module definitions part, the module control function, component types, functions, altsteps, testcases, statement blocks, templates and user-defined named types.
requirements.original: According to clause 5.2, basic scope units of TTCN-3 are module definitions part, module control function, component types, functions, altsteps, test cases, statement blocks, templates and user defined named types.

ambiguity.issue: Uses "test cases" and "user defined named types"; elsewhere the standard uses the keyword-style "testcase" and the glossary term "user-defined type".

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.canonical: A statement block IS NOT named.
requirements.original: Statement blocks have no name and therefore, a __SCOPE__ preprocessing macro used in a statement block refers to the next higher named basic scope unit.

requirements.subject: ent:macro-scope
requirements.canonical: A `__SCOPE__` preprocessing macro used in a statement block refers to the next higher named basic scope unit.
requirements.original: Statement blocks have no name and therefore, a __SCOPE__ preprocessing macro used in a statement block refers to the next higher named basic scope unit.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace every occurrence of `__SCOPE__` with a charstring value determined by the kind of the lowest named scope unit.
requirements.original: A preprocessor or compiler shall replace all occurrences of __SCOPE__ with a charstring value which includes:

ambiguity.issue: "a charstring value which includes" could mean the value consists exactly of the listed name or merely contains it. The examples (D.5-s014) show the value equals the name, so the canonical requirements in items a) to h) use "equal to".
readings: The replacement charstring value SHALL be exactly the listed name.
The replacement charstring value SHALL contain the listed name, possibly with additional text.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the lowest named scope unit is the module definitions part
requirements.canonical: If the lowest named scope unit is the module definitions part, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the module name as a charstring value.
requirements.original: a) the module name, if the lowest named scope unit is the module definitions part;

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the lowest named scope unit is the module control function
requirements.canonical: If the lowest named scope unit is the module control function, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the charstring value "control".
requirements.original: b) "control", if the lowest named scope unit is the module control function;

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the lowest named scope unit is a component type definition
requirements.canonical: If the lowest named scope unit is a component type definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the component type name as a charstring value.
requirements.original: c) a component type name, if the lowest named scope unit is a component type definition;

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the lowest named scope unit is a testcase definition
requirements.canonical: If the lowest named scope unit is a testcase definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the testcase name as a charstring value.
requirements.original: d) a test case name, if the lowest named scope unit is a test case definition;

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the lowest named scope unit is an altstep definition
requirements.canonical: If the lowest named scope unit is an altstep definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the altstep name as a charstring value.
requirements.original: e) an altstep name, if the lowest named scope is an altstep definition;

ambiguity.issue: Uses "lowest named scope" instead of "lowest named scope unit" as in items a) to d).

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the lowest named scope unit is a function definition
requirements.canonical: If the lowest named scope unit is a function definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the function name as a charstring value.
requirements.original: f) a function name, if the lowest named scope is a function definition;

ambiguity.issue: Uses "lowest named scope" instead of "lowest named scope unit".

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the lowest named scope unit is a template definition
requirements.canonical: If the lowest named scope unit is a local or global template definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the template name as a charstring value.
requirements.original: g) a template name, if the lowest named scope is a template definition (local or global); or h) the type name, if the lowest named scope is a user defined named type definition.

ambiguity.issue: Uses "lowest named scope" instead of "lowest named scope unit".

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the lowest named scope unit is a user-defined named type definition
requirements.canonical: If the lowest named scope unit is a user-defined named type definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the type name as a charstring value.
requirements.original: g) a template name, if the lowest named scope is a template definition (local or global); or h) the type name, if the lowest named scope is a user defined named type definition.

ambiguity.issue: Uses "lowest named scope" instead of "lowest named scope unit" and "user defined named type" instead of the glossary term "user-defined type".

requirements.subject: ent:macro-scope
requirements.canonical: The `__SCOPE__` preprocessing macro CANNOT retrieve the names of other kinds of definitions, such as groups or global constants.
requirements.original: NOTE: The __SCOPE__ preprocessing macro cannot be used to retrieve the names of other kinds of definitions, like for example names of groups of definitions or names of global constants.

non_requirement.reason: introductory statement of the annex content
